note: Data question -> chart. 'max' is the point where the chart stops working and the fallback takes over.

charts.question: How did a value change over time?
charts.avoid_when: fewer than four time points (show the numbers) or no time axis
charts.max: five series before it tangles; beyond that, small multiples
charts.a11y: distinguish series by line style and direct labels, not colour alone; offer the data table

charts.question: How do categories compare in size?
alternatives: dot plot when bars are all similar
charts.avoid_when: the categories are ordered in time (use a line)
charts.max: about 15 bars; more needs a horizontal bar or a searchable table
charts.a11y: start the value axis at zero, label bars directly

charts.question: Who is top or bottom?
alternatives: slope chart for rank change between two dates
charts.avoid_when: differences are too small to see; show exact values instead
charts.max: top 10-20 with an 'other' row
charts.a11y: put the rank number in text, keep reading order equal to visual order

charts.question: What share does each part make up?
charts.best: Stacked bar (100%) or a single bar split into parts
alternatives: donut with at most five slices
charts.avoid_when: parts do not add to a meaningful whole, or there are more than five parts
charts.max: five parts; group the rest as 'other'
charts.a11y: label each segment with name and percent; avoid adjacent hues that collapse under colour blindness

charts.question: How are values spread?
alternatives: strip or beeswarm for under 200 points
charts.avoid_when: the audience needs one headline number (give the median and range)
charts.max: box plots for more than five groups
charts.a11y: state the median and range in the caption

charts.question: Do two measures move together?
alternatives: bubble chart for a third measure
binned heatmap for thousands of points
charts.avoid_when: one variable is time (use a line)
charts.max: about 2,000 points before overplotting; then bin or use transparency
charts.a11y: describe the relationship in words; do not imply causation in the title

charts.question: Where do people drop off between steps?
charts.best: Horizontal bars per step with step-to-step conversion labelled
charts.avoid_when: steps are not sequential or users can enter mid-way
charts.max: about seven steps
charts.a11y: write both the count and the percent of the previous step

charts.question: Are we on track against a goal?
alternatives: progress bar with the target marked
charts.avoid_when: there is no agreed target
charts.max: one bullet per row; stack rows for many goals
charts.a11y: state actual, target and percent in text; status needs a word, not just a colour

charts.question: Where is this heading?
charts.best: Line with actuals solid, forecast dashed and an uncertainty band
charts.avoid_when: the forecast has no stated method or interval
charts.max: three scenarios
charts.a11y: label where actuals end; describe the interval in text

charts.question: What looks unusual?
charts.best: Line with an expected band and highlighted points outside it
charts.avoid_when: there is no baseline to compare against
charts.max: a handful of flagged points per view
charts.a11y: mark anomalies with a shape as well as colour, and list them below the chart

charts.question: How does a total break down through levels?
charts.best: Indented table with bars, or a treemap for two levels
charts.avoid_when: small parts matter (treemaps hide them)
charts.max: two levels on screen at once
charts.a11y: provide an expandable tree with the same numbers

charts.question: How does volume move between states?
charts.avoid_when: there are more than about 30 links
charts.max: two to three stages
charts.a11y: offer a from-to table; do not rely on ribbon colour

charts.question: Where is it happening?
charts.best: Choropleth for rates, proportional symbols for counts
alternatives: sorted bar by region when location shape is irrelevant
charts.avoid_when: big empty regions dominate the visual weight; use a bar chart
charts.max: one measure per map
charts.a11y: provide the ranked region table; use a sequential palette that works in greyscale

charts.question: When does activity happen?
charts.avoid_when: exact values matter more than the pattern
charts.max: one year per view
charts.a11y: sequential single-hue scale with a legend and tooltips that read the value

charts.question: What changed between two points?
charts.best: Waterfall for contributions to a change; slope or dumbbell chart for before/after
charts.avoid_when: there are more than two time points (use a line)
charts.max: about 12 steps in a waterfall
charts.a11y: use + and - signs and words, not only green and red

charts.question: How did a price trade within each period?
alternatives: line of closing price for casual users
charts.avoid_when: the audience is not trading; a close-price line is clearer
charts.max: a few hundred candles per view
charts.a11y: up/down by fill and outline, not only red/green; let users choose the colour convention

charts.question: How are things connected?
charts.avoid_when: more than about 100 nodes are shown at once
charts.max: 100 nodes before it becomes a hairball
charts.a11y: provide a list of each node's connections

charts.question: What is happening right now?
charts.best: Rolling line with a fixed window and the latest value in text
charts.avoid_when: updates are faster than people can read; aggregate per second or minute
charts.max: a fixed window (e.g. last 15 minutes)
charts.a11y: announce threshold breaches politely, not every tick; allow pausing updates

charts.question: What is the one number that matters?
charts.best: Stat tile: value, unit, comparison period and change
charts.avoid_when: the number means nothing without context
charts.max: four to six tiles per row
charts.a11y: write the change as text ('up 4% vs last month'), not just an arrow

charts.question: What happens when, and how long?
charts.best: Gantt or timeline bars on a time axis
charts.avoid_when: dates are uncertain; show quarters, not days
charts.max: about 30 rows before grouping
charts.a11y: list view with start, end and owner as a fallback

charts.question: Do newer groups behave better than older ones?
alternatives: retention curves, one line per cohort
charts.avoid_when: fewer than four cohorts exist
charts.max: about 12 cohorts
charts.a11y: values printed in cells; single-hue sequential scale

charts.question: How sure are we?
alternatives: quantile dot plot for lay audiences
charts.avoid_when: the audience will read the bar ends as hard limits without explanation
charts.max: about 20 estimates
charts.a11y: state the interval and what it means in one sentence
